verdict.root_cause: checkoutservice requests are hanging rather than failing: order-entry lines continue at a steady cadence through 12:05 but the three completion lines (payment, confirmation email, queue write) that previously followed within tens of milliseconds are entirely absent, with no error, warn, timeout or rejection output at all [tr_924e7df4577b]. Its error ratio moves from a flat-zero baseline to a bursty 6.7% mean with 67% peaks and one sustained crossing at 12:02:30 [tr_10a8d40cdea2], the shape of deadlines expiring on stalled calls rather than a ramp. The first missing completion is the payment confirmation, placing the stall at or before the charge call, so the stalled dependency is most likely paymentservice, whose only recorded changes are periodic telemetry-endpoint set/revert pairs by automation, last one 5.2h before onset and already reverted [tr_e9920e3d9337]. No deploy, config edit or flag flip exists on frontend [tr_3accd263f91b] or checkoutservice [tr_9dbf71894e33]; frontend's bursty partial elevation is the caller timing out on that path [tr_1791c8174aec].
verdict.reasoning: Entry-without-completion logging plus total silence on error severity means checkoutservice is waiting, not rejecting or crashing, and it is explicitly still alive and receiving traffic [tr_924e7df4577b]. New-onset, high-variance bursty errors from an exactly-zero baseline fit intermittent deadline expiry and were explicitly found inconsistent with a gradual exhaustion ramp [tr_10a8d40cdea2]. Frontend shows the same partial burst pattern and no outage, consistent with a caller absorbing a slow downstream [tr_1791c8174aec]. bad_deploy and bad_config are demoted because the symptomatic services have zero change records over 24h [tr_3accd263f91b, tr_9dbf71894e33] and the one nearby change touched only a telemetry variable that was reverted 5.2h before onset [tr_e9920e3d9337], so no wrong value is in force at request time.
open_questions: No latency percentiles were returned for any service, so the stall is inferred from log-gap structure rather than measured directly [tr_10a8d40cdea2, tr_1791c8174aec].

paymentservice was never queried for logs or metrics; attribution to it rests on which checkoutservice completion line is missing first, and cartservice/currencyservice/emailservice remain unexcluded.

The checkoutservice log result was truncated to the oldest 8 and newest 32 lines, so the transition from healthy to entry-only logging was never observed [tr_924e7df4577b]; frontend's first change point at 11:53 also predates any examined evidence [tr_1791c8174aec].

alternatives.root_cause: A downstream of checkoutservice other than payment (cart, currency, or email) is the stalled dependency and payment completion is missing only because the call ordering differs from the healthy-window sample.
alternatives.why_not: Same mechanism, weaker localisation: the healthy-window log ordering puts payment first among the missing completions, and no evidence was gathered on the other dependencies either way.

alternatives.root_cause: paymentservice is exhausting a bounded resource (connection pool, threads, or memory), so calls queue and never return.
alternatives.why_not: The error-ratio shape is bursty with many zero intervals rather than a monotonic ramp, which the metrics specialist called inconsistent with gradual exhaustion [tr_10a8d40cdea2]; no saturation metric was collected to support it.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected. The next step is observational, not remedial: query paymentservice logs and metrics (error ratio, request-duration percentiles, in-flight/pending counts) plus the same for cartservice, currencyservice and emailservice over 11:30-12:10, and re-pull the checkoutservice log window untruncated so the healthy-to-entry-only transition is actually seen. A restart proposal becomes checkable once paymentservice shows either a stalled-process signature (rising in-flight count with flat completion rate, or a latency percentile pinned at the caller deadline) or is cleared.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if paymentservice is in fact wedged and a restart would have cleared it within a minute — the cost of abstaining is continued stalled checkouts. It would be shown wrong by the follow-up queries returning a clear paymentservice stall signature (in-flight requests climbing while completions stop, or all payment RPCs sitting at the checkout deadline) with no such signature on cartservice, currencyservice or emailservice. Note also that the effect a restart would need to produce — checkoutservice completion lines (payment, confirmation email, queue write) resuming after each order-entry line, and checkoutservice error ratio returning toward its flat-zero baseline [tr_10a8d40cdea2] — is observable, so the abstention is about evidence, not about unobservability.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is prolonged incident duration: orders are being accepted and hung [tr_924e7df4577b], so every minute without action is more stalled checkouts and possibly duplicate charges on retry. The risk of the action I am declining to propose is larger and asymmetric: restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state, and paymentservice has never been queried for a single log line or metric — the entire attribution rests on which checkoutservice completion line is absent first, from a log result truncated to its oldest 8 and newest 32 lines [tr_924e7df4577b]. No latency percentile or in-flight count was returned for any service [tr_10a8d40cdea2], so 'process wedged' is unmeasured. Restarting paymentservice is irreversible, drops in-flight charge calls (risking charges recorded downstream but never confirmed to checkoutservice), and if the stall is actually in cartservice, currencyservice or emailservice — none of them excluded — it destroys the fault state on an innocent service while the real stall continues, leaving responders with a worse evidence board than they have now. rollback_image and revert_config are also unavailable here: no deploy or image change is recorded for checkoutservice [tr_9dbf71894e33] or frontend [tr_3accd263f91b], and paymentservice's only config edits are automation set/revert pairs already reverted 5.2h before onset [tr_e9920e3d9337], so there is no in-window change to revert. scale_service is unavailable by ADR-0029.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because nothing changes. Had a paymentservice restart been proposed, its blast radius would have been paymentservice for the duration of the container recreate, with checkoutservice — its only inbound caller in this graph — seeing connection resets on in-flight charge calls, propagating to frontend and to loadgenerator's success rate.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical severity with multiple user-facing services failing near-simultaneously and no open incident to attribute it to; this cannot be dismissed as a working world. Shared downstream dependencies of frontend and checkout are plausible but nothing yet distinguishes a fault class.
